title: Test: lessons 1–5
description: HTML, CSS, selectors, box model, positioning. No points: −100 XP per mistake, leaving the test −2000 XP.

questions.prompt: This is the project structure. Which line in index.html links the styles correctly?
questions.code:
project/
├── index.html
└── css/
    └── style.css
questions.explain: The path starts from index.html: the file is in the css folder. The last option has no rel="stylesheet" — the styles won't load.

questions.prompt: A student forgot the slash in the closing tag. How will «Text under the heading» look?
questions.code:
My site

Text under the heading
options: Like a normal paragraph — the mistake only affects the heading
The browser shows an error instead of the page
The text won't appear on the page
Big and bold, like a heading
questions.explain: The second <h1> opens a new heading, the paragraph ends up inside it and becomes big and bold.

questions.prompt: A semicolon is missing in the CSS. What applies to the paragraph?
options: None — the whole rule block breaks
questions.explain: Without ; the browser reads the color value as «red background: blue» — that's invalid, so it skips it entirely. Two properties break, font-size works.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
Text

.a { color: red; } .b { color: blue; }
options: Blue — the .b rule is written last in the CSS
Red — class a is written last in the HTML
Black — the two classes conflict and neither applies
questions.explain: The specificity is equal, so the rule written lower in the CSS wins. The order of classes in the class attribute doesn't matter.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
Hello

#box p { color: red; } .wrap .text { color: green; } p.text { color: blue; }
questions.explain: #box p contains an id — it beats any number of classes.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
Hello

#title { color: red; }
options: Red — id has the highest priority
Red — the CSS file is stronger than HTML
Green — a style in the style attribute beats an id
questions.explain: The style attribute beats any CSS selector except !important.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
Hello

p { color: black !important; } #title { color: red; }
options: Red — an id beats a tag
Red — the rule is written lower
questions.explain: !important beats even an id. That's exactly why it's not recommended.

questions.prompt: Which paragraphs turn red?
questions.code:
1

2

3

4

.card p { color: red; }
questions.explain: A space means «inside at any depth», so 2 too. 4 is inside a section with class card — the parent's tag doesn't matter. 3 is outside the cards.

questions.prompt: Note the space in the selector. Which elements turn red?
questions.code:
A

B

C

div .card { color: red; }
questions.explain: div .card is an element with class card inside a div. A is the div with the class itself, not inside one. To pick A you need div.card without a space.

questions.prompt: box-sizing isn't set (default). How wide is the box from the left border to the right one?
questions.explain: 300 + 20 + 20 (padding) + 5 + 5 (border) = 350. Margin isn't included — it's the space outside the border.

questions.prompt: The same box, but * { box-sizing: border-box; } is added to the CSS. How wide is the text area (content) now?
questions.explain: With border-box, 300px is the whole width. 300 − 40 (padding) − 10 (border) = 250.

questions.prompt: What will the left padding be?
questions.code: .box { padding: 10px 20px 30px; }
options: 0px — there's no value for the left side
questions.explain: Three values: top, left-right, bottom. Left = 20px.

questions.prompt: Where on the page will the yellow be?
options: Under the text and in the padding (and under the dashed border)
Under the text, in the padding and in the margin
questions.explain: The background fills content and padding (and shows under the dashed border). Margin is always transparent.

questions.prompt: How wide will the red background be?
questions.code: Hello span { width: 200px; height: 50px; background: red; }
options: There will be no background at all
The full width of the page
Exactly the width of the word «Hello»
questions.explain: span is inline: width and height don't affect it. You need display: inline-block.

questions.prompt: What happens to box B?
questions.code:
A
B
.a { position: relative; top: 30px; }
options: B stays where it is, A may overlap it
B also moves down 30px together with A
B moves up and takes the space A left
questions.explain: relative only shifts the picture — A keeps its place in the «queue».

questions.prompt: Where will the box move?
options: Nowhere — right doesn't work without left
questions.explain: right: 30px is an offset from the right edge of its own place, so the box moves left.

questions.prompt: The card sits in the middle of the page. Where will the badge end up?
questions.code:
SALE
.card { margin: 200px 0 0 100px; width: 300px; } .badge { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; }
options: In the top right corner of the card
In the top left corner of the card
In the top right corner of the whole page
It stays in its place inside the card
questions.explain: The card has no position: relative, so absolute looks further up and attaches to the whole page.

questions.prompt: The parent has no height and no padding. What will its height be?
questions.code:
Box 100 × 100
.parent { border: 1px solid black; } .child { position: absolute; width: 100px; height: 100px; }
options: 0px — the child «left the queue», the parent doesn't see it
The full height of the page
questions.explain: absolute leaves the flow. For the parent the child seems not to exist — height 0.

questions.prompt: A long page. What happens to the box when you scroll down?
questions.code: .menu { position: sticky; }
options: It sticks to the top of the screen
It sticks to the bottom of the screen
It stays in place like fixed
It scrolls up with the page like a normal box
questions.explain: sticky without top doesn't know where to stick, so it behaves like a normal box.

questions.prompt: A «Back to top» button on a long page. What happens when you scroll down?
options: It always stays in the bottom right corner of the screen
It scrolls up with the page
It sticks to the top of the screen
questions.explain: absolute is tied to the page, not the screen, so it scrolls away. You need fixed.
